messages:
alex_cs: Hi team — ACME reporting intermittent 401s from our /v1/chat endpoint around 2026-03-17T14:03Z. They say there is no request id in the response UI screenshot. Can we get a minimal repro ask?

maria_support: Thanks, Alex. First ask the customer to grab either a HAR (preferred) or a curl that reproduces the failing request. If they can't do HAR, a screenshot of the network panel showing response headers (and time) is useful. 

jordan_eng: Quick checklist to include in the ask: 1) exact timestamp (UTC), 2) failing request headers (Authorization masked ok e.g., Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>), 3) response headers, 4) any SDK logs near the time.

alex_cs: They said mobile (Android WebView) so HAR might be hard. What examples do we give non-technical product folks?

jordan_eng: For mobile: ask them to run a syslog / logcat capture during the failure window and copy lines containing 'req_ref' or 'session'. Example log lines we look for: 
`I/RedwoodSDK: req_ref=rr-0a1b2c status=401 path=/v1/chat duration_ms=210`
`D/Network: rw_session=ses-9f8e7 ttl=...`
If they can’t pull logs, ask them to screen-record the app while reproducing and capture the network panel from a proxy (Charles/Fiddler) if available.

maria_support: If they can run curl, provide this minimal template and ask them to paste output (mask token):
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```
We want the verbose response headers; that usually contains x-rw-req or x-request-id.

alex_cs: What header names should we explicitly ask them to look for?

jordan_eng: Ask them to check for any of these in response headers: `x-rw-req`, `x-redwood-req`, `x-request-id`, `x-rw-session`. Also look for `via` or `x-forwarded-for` if proxying. If none appear, also ask for the entire response body and status code.

maria_support: Console hint: if they have a customer console session, show them Console -> Requests -> filter by time -> copy the 'req_ref' column or click a request row and copy Request ID. Tell them the UI label is 'Request ref' (sometimes under Request details).

alex_cs: Customer can't access console. They did provide a screenshot of the response body only (no headers). Requested next step: ask for a single failing cURL or the HAR. Anything else?

jordan_eng: Also ask for correlation to any backend logs: exact time (seconds precision), region, model name if present. If the call passed through our dedicated gateway we can search by timestamp and IP. If they used a serverless function, ask for the function's outbound IP and timestamp.

maria_support: If they can't capture network traces, have them enable verbose SDK logging for a short window and reproduce: set RW_SDK_LOG=DEBUG (or enable in-app debug toggle) and send us the logs with lines around the request. Provide explicit timeframe to reduce noise.

alex_cs: I'll send the consolidated ask. Quick one: if they paste a token, we should tell them how to mask — e.g., keep first 6 and last 4 characters and replace middle with Xs.

sam_proxybot: [automated] Note: no matching req_ref found in edge logs for 2026-03-17T14:03:00Z-14:06:00Z for ACME IP range. If customer provides client-side req_ref we can do a server-side lookup.

maria_support: Perfect. I'll paste a short template for CS to send: 1) exact UTC timestamp(s); 2) curl or HAR (attach file); 3) response headers screenshot if HAR not available; 4) SDK log snippet with 'req_ref' if present; 5) masked Authorization header; 6) app/platform (iOS/Android/WebView/Electron).

alex_cs: Great, thanks. I'll ping when customer uploads. :thumbsup:
